literal_source_claim_zh: 大于5的奇数可表为三素数之和
literal_source_claim_en: Every odd number greater than five can be represented as a sum of three primes.
source_attribution: Historical origin: Christian Goldbach and Leonhard Euler correspondence, 1742; modern exact proof-source lead: Harald A. Helfgott, arXiv:1312.7748v2
canonical_statement: Every odd integer n greater than five can be expressed as the sum of three primes; the three prime summands need not be distinct.
canonical_claim: For every integer n, if n > 5 and n is odd, then there exist positive primes p, q, and r, not necessarily distinct, such that n = p + q + r.
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: Superseded by the exact elaborated natural target recorded below.

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: forall n : Nat, 5 < n -> Odd n -> exists p q r : Nat, Nat.Prime p and Nat.Prime q and Nat.Prime r and n = p + q + r

domain_and_universes: n p q r : Nat in universe 0; the closed target is a Prop in universe 0 with no implicit typeclass or universe binders. The source's n > 5 restricts its integer input to the positive integers, which correspond uniquely to Nat.

conclusion: There exist p q r : Nat with Nat.Prime p, Nat.Prime q, Nat.Prime r, and n = p + q + r; repetition and the even prime 2 remain permitted.
